x: Frank Abberton and Bill Lucas were fifth and seventh and therefore also received their Surrey colours again.
F.
Gosney of Eastleigh beat Olney the local "crack" in the individual race, but our lads packed well with Tom Clinton 4th, Dick Towndrow 5th, Ted Stimpson 6th and Frank Abberton 7th.
Herbert, 57.50; 10 F.
Stimpson; 27 F.
The following gained A.A.A. standard medals:— F.
Stokell, 31.10; 12 F.
Frank Abberton, also recently married, is now living at Streatham Hill and married life seems to agree with him!
Frank Abberton was the individual winner of the Surrey race and Derrick Burfitt only failed by a couple of yards to repeat this performance in the Middlesex event.
Towndrow; 70, F.

Those who were fortunate enough to get in front of the field over the first mile stayed there, and during the whole race the leading men remained the same, Frank Abberton, Bowering (S.L.H.) and Barry (H.H.H.) fighting for first place, Bill Lucas and Marchant being a few places further back.

Then Frank Abberton tackled the up-hill stage through Redhill and ran a fine race to take us up into 2nd place with a time of 23.9. On the next stage, Jack Brown took us in front and running well clocked 28.7.

Frank Abberton, last year's winner, retired after 10 miles and Bert Mitchell also dropped out owing to leg trouble. Actual times and positions of our men were as follows: 13, Footer, 2 hrs. 55 mins. 46 secs.; 17, Ring, 2.58.48; 22, Smith, 3.3.4; 28, Chantler, 3.5.11; 39, Pearson, 3.10.40; 40, Porter…

Frank Abberton the holder of the individual title was a non-entrant, as he is not doing anything over the country this season, but even without him we were fairly confident of retaining the " Pickett " Cup, which is awarded to the winning team.

…the reason for our dropping off is partly explained when we find runners like Len Herbert, Derrick Burfitt, Bill Lucas, Frank Abberton, Reg Ruddick and Eddie Short not taking part in the big races and although we are a club of considerable numerical strength, it takes time to build up a really stron…

Then they had four home to our three, but Frank Abberton scored 27th to make it four each. But Sutton still had five in before our 5th man (Tom Carter 41st) and then praise be, Tommy Clinton came along in 57th place to complete our scoring six, while Sutton's 6th man finished 65th!
Two former members of winning 'National' C.C. teams have been to our fixtures. On Boxing Day we had DICK TOBIN eyeing the field and FRANK ABBERTON was at the Surrey C.C.
Frank Abberton · Mar 49

Len Herbert was coming through well and Frank Abberton and Tom Clinton were also well placed. Albert Frost unfortunately had a bad time but Tom Carter was running well and eventually became our sixth scoring man with Les Stokell unluckily missing a winner's medal by two places.
On the next stage to Merstham, Ted Stimpson held his place ... then Frank Abberton tackled the uphill stage through Redhill and ran a fine race to take us up to 2nd place.
